name: figures written out are the same figures
a: The survey reached 3 million homes in 12 countries, and 40% replied.
b: Three million homes in twelve countries got the survey; 40% of them answered.

name: a dropped figure and a changed one
a: The trial enrolled 412 patients over 18 months at a cost of 2.5 million euros.
b: The trial enrolled patients over 16 months at a cost of 2.5 million euros.

name: a name moved to the start of a sentence is kept
a: The report was written by Okafor and reviewed in Geneva.
b: Okafor wrote the report, which was then reviewed in Geneva.

name: a name swapped for another
a: The method was first described by Lindqvist in a paper on sampling.
b: The method was first described by Lindgren in a paper on sampling.

name: a lost negation is shown, not counted
a: The effect did not survive the correction, and the authors don't claim it.
b: The effect survived the correction, and the authors don't claim it.

name: most became all
a: Most participants finished at least two sessions.
b: All participants finished two sessions.

name: two hundred and five
a: There were 205 entries and 1,250 votes.
b: There were two hundred and five entries and one thousand two hundred fifty votes.

name: Italian compound numbers
a: Lo studio ha coinvolto 345 persone in 23 città e 1.200 famiglie.
b: Lo studio ha coinvolto trecentoquarantacinque persone in ventitré città e milleduecento famiglie.

name: Italian millions and a decimal comma
a: Il bilancio è di 2,5 milioni, contro i tre milioni dell'anno scorso.
b: Il bilancio è di 2,5 milioni, contro i 3 milioni dell'anno precedente.

name: Italian: a lost name counts, a lost non is shown
a: Secondo Ferraris il modello non funziona sui testi brevi.
b: Secondo gli autori il modello funziona sui testi brevi.

name: Italian sei is a verb on its own
a: Sei sicuro che siano trentasei?
b: Sei certo che siano 36?

name: Spanish tens joined by y
a: Participaron 33 equipos de 7 países durante 1.500 horas.
b: Participaron treinta y tres equipos de siete países durante mil quinientas horas.

name: Spanish: casi todos became todos
a: Casi todos los estudiantes aprobaron, pero ninguno con nota máxima.
b: Todos los estudiantes aprobaron, pero ninguno con nota máxima.

name: Spanish: a figure changed and García lost
a: Según García, el 60% de los encuestados no usa la aplicación.
b: Según el estudio, el 70% de los encuestados no usa la aplicación.

name: capitals are not new names
a: The committee in Brussels did not approve all of the 12 proposals.
b: THE COMMITTEE IN BRUSSELS DID NOT APPROVE ALL OF THE 12 PROPOSALS.

name: list numbers are not facts
a:
Three steps:
1. Measure the room.
2. Buy the paint.
b:
Three steps:
1. Buy the paint.
2. Measure the room.
3. Clean the brushes.

name: Title Case headings are style, not names
a:
## Preservation of Local History

The museum opened in 1990.

Opportunities for Young Readers

It lends 4,000 books a year.
b:
## Keeping Local Memory Alive

The museum opened in 1990.

Chances for Young People

It lends 4,000 books a year.

name: a curly apostrophe is the same name
a: The Landlord's reply came late, and I am still waiting.
b: The Landlord’s reply came late, and I’m still waiting.

name: a name inside a sentence after a heading still counts
a:
# Report

The study was led by Okonjo in Accra.
b:
# Report

The study was led by Mensah in Accra.

name: a colon opens a clause
a: Tip 3: Putting the lid on keeps the soup warm for 20 minutes.
b: Tip 3: Closing the lid keeps the soup warm for 20 minutes.

name: a bold label is a heading
a: - **Drafting Proposals:** the committee met in Rome twice.
b: - **Writing Ideas:** the committee met in Rome twice.

name: possessives, plurals and hyphens are the same name
a: Amazon's sales rose, and the RRSP rules for a Tax Free account changed.
b: Sales at Amazon rose, and the RRSPs rules for a Tax-Free account changed.

name: a capitalised function word is not a name
a: We met them (During the summer) in Lisbon.
b: We met them in Lisbon in the summer.

name: Spanish escasas and muy pocas are both few
a: Las lluvias fueron escasas en el norte.
b: Las lluvias fueron muy pocas en el norte.
